sections.title: Basic negation
sections.content: *nem* makes a statement negative. In these short patterns it comes before the part being negated: Nem *vagyok* Meg. Nem tea.

*Nem* is doing double duty: it's both the standalone "no" and the "not" that negates a word. English keeps those as two separate words; Hungarian just reuses one. So once you've learned *nem*, you've effectively learned two English words for the price of one. Word order also shifts what's being denied: *Nem vagyok Meg* just denies being Meg, while *Nem Meg vagyok* puts the stress right on the name — "it's not Meg that I am."
